name: Jade Dubois

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am a researcher with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers stay confidential. Tell me about a regular shift.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and a junior agent on calls and chats. I finished secondary school, and I am still learning the account rules, so I use AI every day to sort the case notes before I answer. It sometimes makes me quicker; it also invents a tidy reason for a charge that never happened.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is home like after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Ben and I have two school-age children and a mortgage. Ben works at a garden centre, my pay is typical for this job, and we have about four months of expenses saved. There are some other centres nearby, but a change has to work for the whole household, not just my curiosity.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues a small tool is fine if agents can show where an answer came from. I would offer to share the mistakes I spot so no one has to find them twice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my junior job stays for now, though I am still below the experienced agents on speed. Four months saved means we can fix a car without missing the mortgage, but it is not permission to gamble. I want to use the quiet year to get better at the account rules.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep using the AI note sorter and check its suggested charge reasons against the customer record. I would ask an experienced agent to walk me through one billing error each Friday. In the first year, Ben and I would keep our four-month reserve and pay the mortgage on the same schedule.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about my own skill gap, even if the technology levels off. I am glad the clock slows enough for me to learn.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What mistake would you share first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The sorter once labelled a late fee as a payment failure when the date had been entered wrong. I would put that example in the team notes with the customer details removed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for a course now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. A colleague can show me the rules on the job, and I would only pay for a course if it led to a posted role we could afford to pursue.

think: My junior role probably stays, but I am still **slow** beside experienced agents.
Our four-month **reserve** is for household surprises, not a speculative course.
do: Keep sorting **notes** and checking charge reasons.
Learn one **billing error** from an experienced agent weekly.
Keep our **mortgage payments** and reserve steady.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the floor the easy calls may go first, so junior agents need a paid path into the harder ones. I would join the union meeting and bring examples of bot errors that send people back into the queue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can see my own shifts falling before I master the difficult cases. Being keen on AI does not make me safe if software answers the calls I handle. Four months saved buys us time, but Ben cannot carry the mortgage alone indefinitely.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would ask for a paid place testing the new answer system and keep a log of wrong handoffs. I would attend the union meeting to seek paid practice on disputed accounts for junior agents. In the first year, if my hours fall I would apply to a posted paid quality support role at this centre or another nearby, provided its hours and wage cover my mortgage share.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, and I also want to see how the new system works. I cannot treat a trial as a job offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the union ask for in your view?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A posted training schedule, paid hours to learn and a clear wage for the jobs that follow. I would ask other juniors to bring their rosters too, so the hours are not just my story.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Ben say about a job across town?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ben would ask what it pays after travel. We can manage a longer trip if the wage covers the mortgage and child care, but not for a better-sounding title.

think: My own **shifts** could fall before I improve on difficult account calls.
My AI interest cannot replace a **mortgage wage** if junior shifts disappear.
do: Test the new **answer system** on paid time.
Join the **union meeting** with junior rosters.
Apply for **posted paid quality work** only if offered wage and hours cover mortgage share, travel and childcare.

fieldNote: She does not confuse tool enthusiasm with **job safety**.
Union action is shared through junior **rosters**.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues AGI by 2028 could answer our calls before a junior has time to build a second skill. I would ask the union to seek written notice and funded routes to named jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my call job could disappear in 2028 despite all my AI practice. Robots around 2031 are later and do not keep a headset occupied. Our four-month reserve is useful, but a mortgage and two children can eat it quickly if several centres stop hiring.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would join the union meeting on notice and ask the supervisor which paid audit jobs actually exist. I would save examples of wrong AI charge decisions without customer names and apply to posted paid review vacancies while still earning. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, if my post ends I would take a paid role whose hours cover the mortgage, or use the reserve to search while Ben and I cut nonessential spending.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed by the speed, but I can still move. The worst part is the thought that every nearby centre may put the same notice on its door.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you study for an audit job now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if a real vacancy requires it and the employer funds the study time or we can pay without touching mortgage money. I would not buy a general AI certificate because an advert frightened me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say we may skip our weekend outings for a while if my shifts end. I would not ask them to plan their lives around a date I cannot control.

I would ask for funded routes into **named paid jobs**.
think: My call job could go in **2028**.
I fear our **four-month reserve** may run out during a shared hiring freeze.

Apply for **posted paid review** while employed; after a cut accept only offered hours covering the mortgage.

fieldNote: She knows robots arrive later than the **screen threat**.
She keeps customer details out of her **error examples**.
Study requires a real vacancy and safe **funding**.

steps.text: Join the union meeting to seek notice and funded routes to named jobs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team five years is time to build a real quality job, with paid training for the juniors who spot mistakes now. I would ask the union to check that the new role has a wage on the notice board.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still think most calls go when AGI comes in 2031. I could learn to audit bad answers by then, and my four-month reserve lets me take a careful step without risking next month's mortgage. Robots around 2034 are not my first deadline.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would request paid audit practice and complete the centre’s service-check course if it is funded and linked to a posted role. I would keep logging wrong charge decisions and attend union meetings on junior training. In the first year after 2031, if calls end I would apply for a paid audit vacancy with hours that cover the mortgage; otherwise I would keep any paid centre work while searching nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious but purposeful. Five years gives me enough time to see whether auditing is a real job or just an extra task.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would you ask to assess your audit work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the quality supervisor to check a sample of my cases and tell me what I missed. I need evidence of skill, not a badge printed from a course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the family for the role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for a written paid offer after we calculate housing, school travel and Ben’s work. I would not move the children on a promise of interviews.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues a decade gives us time to build an appeals job with proper pay rather than patching errors for free. I would keep the union involved because juniors need a way in, not just senior agents.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 53 in 2036, and I would rather be reviewing decisions than answering the same routine chat. I do not know what we will still owe on the mortgage then. Robots around 2039 come later than the change to our screens.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep my shifts and ask for paid time each month to learn to audit AI charge decisions with the quality team. I would add to our reserve and pursue a funded qualification only if a posted paid appeals role requires it. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, if the role exists I would apply at a wage and hours that cover the mortgage; if not, I would search nearby while continuing any paid work I have.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the old queue ending, but I can picture another place in the centre. Ten years gives me time to prove I can do the review work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you put in an application?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A record of corrected charges, repeat calls avoided and the rules I used, with names removed. The numbers should show I did more than click a tool.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if nobody posts an appeals role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would keep earning and look at other centres. I would not borrow for a qualification without a wage on the other side.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. A real paid audit vacancy, funded training tied to it and written notice would help us keep the mortgage current while I move. I can learn fast, but our four months saved is not an endless bridge.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who gets credit for finding a machine error before the customer pays for it. Junior agents already catch machine errors, but the dashboard only counts how fast we close the chat.

headlineQuote: Junior agents already catch machine errors, but the dashboard only counts how fast we close the chat.
portrait: Jade is a **43-year-old junior** contact centre agent with secondary school education and typical pay.
She shares a mortgage and two school-age children with **Ben** and has four months of expenses saved.
She uses AI **daily**, still learns account rules and has some other centres nearby.
She joins **union meetings** and seeks paid audit work with posted wages and funded training.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase her calls while nearby centres also stop hiring.
whatWouldHelp: A real paid **audit vacancy**, funded training linked to it and written notice would help.
